title: Decision storyboard: narrative-driven constraint composer for caching & batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: High-level story-driven UX concept for a Constraint Composer panel in the Redwood Console. The composer presents a linear, narrative storyboard that helps operators understand why specific caching and batching suggestions are made, lets them author constraints (cost, latency, quality), preview downstream effects on SLOs, and simulate rollbacks. This ticket covers prototypes, microcopy, acceptance criteria, and a usability validation plan.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive storyboard prototype (Figma) demonstrates three scenario lanes: latency-first, cost-first, and hybrid with live parameter sliders
Users can author 3 types of constraints: hard limits (max tokens per request), soft targets (preferred batch size), and exception rules (skip caching for X routes) in the composer
Preview panel shows estimated delta for cost, p95 latency, and normalized output-quality score after applying constraints
Composer displays a single-line rollback recipe and exports a JSON policy compatible with runtime-1.22 rollout API
Microcopy reviewed and signed off by PM and Accessibility reviewer (contrast, aria hints)
Prototype tested with 6 platform engineers in guerrilla usability sessions with recorded task success and qualitative notes
design_notes: We intentionally use a linear 'storyboard' metaphor instead of a modal or wizard to reduce perceived complexity for operators who want to reason about trade-offs. Each storyboard step contains a short rationale card (why this suggestion exists), an editable control, and a live mini-simulation. Simulation uses simplified heuristics (based on recent route distributions) rather than live queries to avoid exposing PII. The preview card displays three KPIs with colored deltas and an uncertainty band. The composer can output a compact policy snippet and a human-readable rollback recipe.
decisions: Use storyboard layout rather than modal wizard to make sequence of trade-offs explicit
Expose three constraint types only on initial launch to limit UI complexity
Simulate using anonymized recent telemetry instead of live replay to respect privacy and to keep response snappy
Provide one-click export to both JSON policy and plaintext rollback instructions
tradeoffs: Favoring narrative clarity may consume more vertical screen space on dashboards. We mitigate by offering a collapsed compact view and an inline toggle to switch to a condensed editor. Simulation accuracy is intentionally approximate to preserve performance and privacy; callouts in the UI will surface confidence bands and link to the detailed estimator.
usability_plan: Recruit 6 internal platform engineers + 2 SEs from pilot customers. Tasks: (1) apply latency-first preset and save policy, (2) set an exception for a single route and preview impact, (3) export rollback recipe and interpret it. Capture time-on-task, success/failure, and verbal walkthroughs. Run two 45-minute sessions with recorded screens.
metrics: Task success rate >= 85% in internal tests
Median time to create & export policy < 8 minutes
At least 80% of testers find simulation helpful (Likert 4/5)
next_steps: Handoff to frontend for interaction spec (8/08)
Implement prototype telemetry stub in staging for simulation (ENG)
review_comments: PM: Include explicit indication of which routes will be affected by a constraint (suggested: spotlight list)
Infra: Simulator needs a sampling guarantee; work with Observability to expose aggregated histograms rather than raw samples
Design: Add microcopy explaining confidence band calculation and link to docs
